instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: A poor first season in a chaotic, relegated club, but an Argentina centre-back whose ability was plainly above what the year showed.
A World Cup final starter three years earlier; still a good, versatile top-flight defender at 28.
A World Cup and European Championship winner arriving at thirty-three; the legs had gone but the touch and passing were still a division above anything else at the club.
Twelve goals from fifteen starts as a 22-year-old; a real step up from the fringe player of the previous season rather than a scoring fluke.
Seventeen and already extraordinarily quick, but a long way from a finished footballer.
Comfortably the most technically gifted player in a relegated West Brom side; a capped Wales playmaker with genuine top-flight passing, held back by inconsistency rather than ability.
At twenty-six, in the conversation for the best attacking full back in the world — level with Dani Alves 2009/10 rather than above him.
Rated for the player he was in 1998/99 — aggressive, ill-disciplined and frequently exposed — not for the Inter and Italy defender he became five years later.
Halfway between the exposed twenty-four-year-old at Everton and the World Cup winner of 2006/07: an Inter starter when fit, still rash.
Eight years on from Everton he is a World Cup winner and a starter in a Scudetto side — a genuinely different, more disciplined defender, hence the rise.
A quick, sensible young full-back at Arsenal; sound rather than good.
Nineteen goals in a seventh-placed side and the club’s player of the season; the one year he was fit throughout.
Loaned back to Blackburn with the knee gone: seven starts, no goals, and none of the movement of 2007/08.
A cruciate rupture in December took most of the season; rated on the player, who at twenty-five was already the best passer in Spain.
Thirty-four, nineteen starts and a rotation player in his final season — eight points below the 2009/10 peak, which is what the five years cost him.

Twenty league goals at twenty-six, playing off Cassano rather than as the false nine Spalletti later built around him — which is why the trait differs from the 2006/07 row. Elite, two short of that peak.
Twenty-six league goals and the European Golden Shoe as Spalletti’s false nine, months after winning the World Cup — the best season of his career.
A January loan from Roma who started strongly; a genuinely gifted centre-forward, already a fixture for Egypt, with an obvious temperament problem.
